A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAM-Decoding and contain readable methods, equations, results, figures, and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched despite substantial rewriting and expanded appendices.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original Vicuna-7B experiments on Spec-Bench, HumanEval, MBPP, and HAGRID, including component and hyperparameter analyses.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B–C report original benchmark results, additional model and GPU evaluations, and timing and draft-selection analyses.

M1.justification: v1 retrieves contiguous token sequences from both automata. v3 adds frequency-based top-k successors and Prim-style tree drafting for the static automaton (Sections 3.1–3.2, Appendix A). Section 3.3 also changes the stated dynamic update order from expansion-before-transfer to transfer-before-expansion, although v3's introduction retains the earlier description.

E1.justification: MBPP, evaluated in v1 Table 2, is absent from v3. Spec-Bench's six tasks, HumanEval, and HAGRID remain, so code generation and the other principal task domains are retained. Additional model sizes and GPUs change configurations rather than dataset coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds PIA and removes the original EAGLE comparator while retaining EAGLE-2. It also adds Lookahead and REST comparisons on the retained HumanEval and HAGRID benchmarks, where v1 Table 2 included only PLD among retrieval baselines. These changes substantially revise the comparative evidence across the principal experiments.

E3.justification: v3 adds Llama3-8B-Instruct, Vicuna-13B, Vicuna-33B, and an A800 evaluation to v1's Vicuna-7B/A6000 setup. It specifies 16-token drafts for code datasets instead of the previous 40-token default and zero bias without an auxiliary method. Its stated auxiliary defaults also replace v1's explicit Token Recycling tree override; this documents a protocol revision without proving which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The component ablation changes from removing three components of SAM-Decoding[T] to removing static or dynamic automata from standalone SAM-Decoding, with PLD as a control. Appendix C adds inference-stage timing, draft-source usage and acceptance analyses, and a GPU transfer check. The threshold study remains, while the draft-size plot drops its accepted-token series.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Both primarily present point estimates of speed, throughput, and mean accepted tokens.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive model/device results and removes MBPP and original EAGLE entries. Reported Spec-Bench SAM-Decoding[E2] speedup changes from 2.49× to 2.58×. The HumanEval comparison reverses from 3.27× versus EAGLE-2's 3.30× to 3.35× versus 3.24×. Method and code-draft setting revisions limit attribution of these differences to a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: The amortized O(1), worst-case O(L) state-transfer proof is retained from v1 Appendix A.2 in v3 Appendix A.3. v3 adds frequency-ratio transition probabilities and a maximum-spanning-tree drafting formulation, but no new central complexity theorem.

C1.justification: The central claims about exact suffix matching, constant amortized retrieval cost, and adaptive integration remain. v3 replaces the broad outperform-all framing with explicit standalone retrieval-baseline comparisons and claimed incremental EAGLE-2 gains across model sizes. Its conclusion also explicitly includes contextual question answering.

C2.justification: New Section 7 identifies corpus diversity and cross-model mismatch, heuristic draft selection, and limited benchmark realism as specific limitations. v3 also adds a GPU-work explanation for the draft-size tradeoff and revises the HumanEval interpretation from reduced model-based throughput toward limited gains attributed to less copying during code generation.

D1.justification: v3 adds root-state and frequency initialization details plus top-k and priority-queue drafting pseudocode. It specifies Transformers 4.46.1, clarifies that the retrieval corpus uses Vicuna-generated outputs, and identifies environment-specific baseline comparisons. Conversely, v1's task-specific corpus instructions and explicit Token Recycling override disappear. The repository link remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Zhao et al.'s PIA work and removes references associated with MBPP, PagedAttention, and SGLang. It groups Lookahead with retrieval methods while distinguishing Token Recycling's use of token distributions. The broader positioning around retrieval-based speculative decoding remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, background and method explanations are extensively edited, and related work is condensed. A separate limitations section and additional experimental appendices reorganize the narrative. Authorship, affiliations, and terminology also change.

P2.justification: v3 reorganizes the main results into a combined table and radar charts, redraws the workflow and draft-size displays, and adds automaton, model-scaling, timing, and draft-usage figures. Additional appendix tables and algorithms substantially change the visual organization, alongside a different document template and float placement.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evidence for generalizability beyond v1's single backbone/device through additional model families, sizes, and GPU testing. Profiling, draft-source analyses, implementation detail, and specific limitations also make the method easier to assess. These gains outweigh the loss of MBPP and original EAGLE comparisons, although v3 still needs corrections to conflicting SAM update descriptions and Section 4's EAGLE-2 task scores, which disagree with Figure 5.
